newsitem.title: USA: U.S. expects to give Taiwan president transit visa.
newsitem.headline: U.S. expects to give Taiwan president transit visa.

text.p: Despite a likely hostile reaction from China, the U.S. State Department said on Wednesday it expected to issue a transit visa to allow Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui to pass through the United States in September.
Spokesman James Foley said Lee had applied to transit through Honolulu on Sept. 4-5 and Sept. 17-18 on his way to and from a conference in Panama.
"The U.S. expects to authorise these transits," Foley told reporters.

But he said Washington expected Lee to respect the conditions under which such visas are issued -- a coded way of saying that the Taiwanese leader would be expected to refrain from political activities during his stopovers.
Taiwan announced on July 14 that Lee would be seeking a transit visa for his first footfall on U.S. soil since a 1995 visit to New York that drew a furious response from Beijing.
China temporarily downgraded its U.S. ties, froze semi-official talks with Taiwan and launched months of menacing war games near the island.
The United States, which does not maintain official ties with Taipei, had said in April that Lee was eligible for a visa to transit Hawaii or the U.S. west coast on his way to Panama.
The day after the Taiwanese announcement, China called on the United States to ensure that Lee would not conduct activities harmful to Chinese unity with his transit.

"We hope the American side ... will not allow key Taiwan political figures to create 'two Chinas' or 'one China, one Taiwan' or conduct activities to split the motherland under the name of transiting the country," a foreign ministry spokesman said in Beijing.
China and Taiwan have been split since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949. Beijing regards Taiwan as a rebel province and seeks to isolate its leaders from the international arena.
Panama, once of just 30 states that recognise Taipei rather than Beijing, has invited Lee to attend a Sept. 7-10 conference for users of the Panama Canal Zone.
Most air routes linking East Asia to Central America include stopovers on the U.S. west coast or Hawaii.
